title: Composed supervisory control: Fair two-client resource arbiter with emergency lockout -> Duty-standby pump feedback failover

inputs.name: A_RequestA
inputs.description: Subsystem A: Client A requests the resource

inputs.name: A_RequestB
inputs.description: Subsystem A: Client B requests the resource

inputs.name: A_Done
inputs.description: Subsystem A: Current client releases the resource

outputs.name: A_GrantA
outputs.description: Subsystem A: Resource grant to client A

outputs.name: A_GrantB
outputs.description: Subsystem A: Resource grant to client B

outputs.name: A_Busy
outputs.description: Subsystem A: Resource has an active owner

outputs.name: A_Turn
outputs.description: Subsystem A: Tie-break preference: 1 A, 2 B

outputs.name: B_FailoverActive
outputs.description: Subsystem B: Standby is serving demand

outputs.name: B_Failure
outputs.description: Subsystem B: Latched inability to establish running feedback

scan.initialization: fresh function-block instance for every test case

assumptions: The function block is called exactly once per PLC scan.
Inputs are sampled at scan start and outputs are checked at scan end.
Each test starts from a fresh function-block instance.
The runtime scan period is 100 ms.
Pump feedback is sampled at scan start.
Subsystem A executes before the supervisory latch and subsystem B within each scan.
Requirements inherited from subsystem B apply only while SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE.
When subsystem B is isolated, its externally visible outputs take their type-safe defaults.

requirements.text: Subsystem A shall satisfy: A_GrantA and A_GrantB shall never be TRUE simultaneously.
Subsystem A shall satisfy: When idle, a single request shall receive the resource; simultaneous requests shall follow A_Turn.
Subsystem A shall satisfy: A_Done shall release the current grant before a new owner is selected on a later scan.
Subsystem A shall satisfy: After A completes A_Turn shall prefer B, and after B completes A_Turn shall prefer A.
requirements.property: G((A_Done AND A_GrantA)->X(A_Turn=2)) AND G((A_Done AND A_GrantB)->X(A_Turn=1))

requirements.text: Subsystem A shall satisfy: A_Emergency shall immediately revoke all grants and latch A_LockedOut.
Subsystem A shall satisfy: A_Reset shall clear A_LockedOut only while A_Emergency and both requests are FALSE.
While SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE, subsystem B shall satisfy: A new B_Demand shall command the available duty pump, or the standby if the duty pump is unavailable.
While SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE, subsystem B shall satisfy: If the commanded pump lacks feedback for 300 ms, control shall transfer to an available standby pump.
While SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE, subsystem B shall satisfy: Both run commands shall never be TRUE simultaneously.
While SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE, subsystem B shall satisfy: B_Failure shall latch if B_Demand cannot be served by an available pump with feedback after failover.
While SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE, subsystem B shall satisfy: B_Demand FALSE shall stop both pumps; B_Reset may clear B_Failure only with B_Demand FALSE.
A TRUE A_GrantA shall latch CrossReady unless CrossReset is TRUE in the same scan.
CrossReset shall have priority, clear CrossReady, and isolate every subsystem-B output to its type-safe default.
Once set, CrossReady shall remain TRUE after the subsystem-A signal falls, until a later CrossReset scan.
Subsystem B may execute only while SubsystemBEnable and CrossReady are TRUE; CrossBlocked is TRUE exactly when SubsystemBEnable is requested without CrossReady.

provenance.origin: deterministic ordered composition of independently specified base behaviors
